claim_as_stated: 7.37 million pathways
detail: Exact on NHS England's headline basis (reported + carry-forward for RHQ, RA9, RK9, RNS). On my Two Maps measure the list is 7,158,164, 211,936 lower.

claim_as_stated: up 41,848 on July
detail: Exact on the headline basis. The 15,369 gap between the bases is entirely the change in estimated trusts: NMG -24,567; RNS +39,936 (Northampton newly estimated; Cora resubmitted in August).

claim_as_stated: the fourth rise in five months
detail: Month-on-month rises in the list, April to August 2026. On my measure non-submitters break the run.

claim_as_stated: ~113,000 waiting more than 52 weeks
detail: Over-52 headline rebuilt exactly by carrying forward each missing trust's base-month 52+ count (gate B).

claim_as_stated: median wait 12.2 weeks
basis: reported (NHS England publishes no headline-basis median)
detail: Rebuilt by interpolation in the weekly bands; matches the Overview series in all 17 months.

claim_as_stated: a record 4.7 million treatments, procedures and appointments across June to August
claimed_by: article brief (NHS England press office wording)
detail: Rebuilt exactly from the Overview series, and identical to NHS England's press figure. It is the highest of all 19 full June-Augusts in the series (2008-2026), 127,159 above 2025. Wording: these are COMPLETED RTT PATHWAYS, which include clock stops other than treatment, so 'pathways completed' is the accurate phrase.

claim_as_stated: its highest recorded quarter of elective activity
detail: A record for a summer, not for any three months: Nov 2025-ending window 4,831,794; Mar 2026-ending window 4,797,102 were higher.

claim_as_stated: Sheffield sends no RTT data, yet is the lowest trust on 62-day cancer (51.8%)
rebuilt: 51.8% Jun-Aug 2026 pooled, rank 1 of 136; 62-day reported in 17 of 17 months
detail: Two separate collections. RTT has been withheld since its July 2025 EPR go-live (data-quality issues, per NHS England's notice); its cancer return kept coming, with no repeated month (0 identical consecutive months) and no mention in either release's missing/partial annex. Its 62-day rate was 47.4-53.8% in Apr-Jun 2025, before the RTT gap, and 42.6-57.5% across all 17 months: low throughout, not a post-EPR artefact. Context to check before use: a trust hosting a specialist cancer centre receives late inter-trust referrals.

claim_as_stated: the 12 November publication replaces it
detail: From gov.uk's RTT announcement for September 2026 (published 9 Oct 2026, read 17 Oct 2026). The brief cited the A&E announcement; cite the RTT one.

claim_as_stated: +7,000 more people waiting over a year (title)
detail: No single month gives +7,000. The nearest span is June→August on the headline basis (+7,628), which is two months.

claim_as_stated: over-52-week group grew by roughly six per cent
detail: About 6-7% only over two months (May→Jul +6.3%, Jun→Aug +7.2%); +20.1% since March 2026.

claim_as_stated: the list grew by well under one per cent
detail: Holds on both bases.

claim_as_stated: indexed April 2025 = 100: one line near flat, one climbing away
rebuilt: tail -40.4%, list -0.3% (headline); panel and reported agree
detail: On the proposed index the tail FELL about 40% while the list stayed flat. The chart as briefed would show the opposite of the argument.

claim_as_stated: the total and the tail move at different rates, 'like separate queues'
rebuilt: since Mar 2026: tail +20.1% vs list +3.7% (headline); panel +20.9% vs +3.7%; reported +18.7% vs +2.0%
detail: Holds from March 2026 on every basis; the tail grew faster in 5 of 5 months. Over 18 weeks tracks the list, not the tail. Before March the tail was shrinking faster than the list.

claim_as_stated: (implicit) the March 2026 low is a real starting point
rebuilt: revision moved Mar-26 by -44 pathways (1 trust)
detail: Not a revision artefact. A system-wide year-end low at the deadline for the 65% / <1% targets (March: 65.3% within 18 weeks, met; 1.33% over 52, missed), with elevated long-wait exits and unreported removals. Say so if the window starts there.
primary_file: superseded + revised Mar26 full CSVs; Overview; 2025/26 planning guidance (web page)

claim_as_stated: 6.24 million patients
detail: An estimate, not a count: the WLMDS ratio of unique NHS numbers to pathways (week ending 30 Aug) times monthly pathways. The ratio appears only as a result; the press notice rounds it to 85:100 (which would give 6.26m).

claim_as_stated: ~1.1 million people on more than one pathway
rebuilt: 1,127,829 surplus pathways = upper bound on people with 2+
detail: Exact as 'more pathways than patients'. As people it is a ceiling: if anyone holds 3+ pathways the true count is lower (e.g. ≥563,915 if nobody holds more than 3). No published file gives the distribution.

claim_as_stated: most coverage reports the pathway figure as if it were people
detail: A claim about the media, not the data. Needs a review of coverage. NHS England's own notice says 'Some patients are on multiple pathways'.

claim_as_stated: referred in August 2026 … one joins the 113,000 waiting more than a year
rebuilt: a pathway starting in Aug 2026 is at most 4.4 weeks old at month end
detail: Nobody referred in August 2026 can be in the over-52-week count for August 2026. The vignette needs someone referred in or before August 2025.

claim_as_stated: treated inside twelve weeks, because the median wait is 12.2
rebuilt: 12.2 = median of people still waiting; completed medians Aug-26: admitted 13.0 wks, non-admitted 8.8 wks
detail: The 12.2 weeks is a snapshot of the waiting stock, not the time to treatment for a new referral. For the time people actually waited, use the completed-pathway medians.

claim_as_stated: 62-day performance 71.9 per cent
detail: Provisional: August 2025 moved +0.22 pp when finalised.

claim_as_stated: against an 85 per cent standard
detail: 'Operational Standard = 85% from Q3 2023/24'.

claim_as_stated: improved year on year
rebuilt: +2.78 pp like for like (69.1% → 71.9%); +2.56 pp vs final
detail: Like for like = provisional Aug 2025 (first published 9 Oct 2025) against provisional Aug 2026.

claim_as_stated: still thirteen points short
detail: Only 13 of 136 trusts meet 85% (Jun-Aug 2026 pooled); 109 are clearly below it.

claim_as_stated: 28-day faster diagnosis 78.6 per cent
detail: Provisional.

claim_as_stated: against an 80 per cent operational target
detail: 'Operational Standard = 80% from Q1 2026/27'.

claim_as_stated: a target missed by under two points
detail: Year on year +3.95 pp like for like; 78 of 140 trusts now meet 80%.

claim_as_stated: still means tens of thousands told late
rebuilt: 58,673 late; 54,732 permitted by the 80% standard; 3,941 beyond it
detail: The count is right, but most of it is what the standard allows. The miss itself is 3,941 people in August, close to 62-day's 3,657.

claim_as_stated: figures consistent with my earlier RTT pieces (Two Maps measure)
detail: This pipeline reproduces Two Maps' July figures exactly. Any headline-basis figure quoted must be labelled as such.

claim_as_stated: basis for national figures in the article
rebuilt: headline basis (NHS England's, incl. estimates for non-submitting trusts)
detail: National England figures are quoted on NHS England's headline basis. Two Maps used the reported basis because it joined provider-level data, where estimates can't be allocated to trusts. The since-March divergence holds on headline, reported and constant-panel bases (row on 'separate queues').
